newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's 1996 grain crop could hit record - official.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's 1996 grain crop could hit record - official.

text.p: Sweden's 1996 grain crop could reach the record high of 1990 after a better-than-expected harvest, the national farmers' cooperative Landmannen said.
Spokeswoman Margareta Minser said the harvest, now nearing its end, looked set to exceed six million tonnes and could reach the record of 6.39 million in 1990.
The group had estimated at the beginning of the harvest a crop of 5.62 million tonnes.
Last year the crop was 4.79 million.
"It seems the quality of the crop and the quantities have been better than we thought," Minser told Reuters.
She said about 10 percent more land had been sown to grain this year, with the crop covering a total of 1.2 million hectares.
But the harvest was later than normal, delayed by a cool spring and rainy summer.
Domestic demand averages four million tonnes a year and the rest of the crop -- mainly spring barley, winter wheat and oats -- is exported.
